mbm-1801.clue: My loudest trick begins with an empty matchbox.
mbm-1801.quote: I tell the audience there is a cricket inside and slide the drawer open. My brother, hiding behind the curtains, makes one perfect chirp. Sometimes the real crickets answer him.

mbm-1802.clue: My granddad keeps the best dance cards.
mbm-1802.quote: Before our first foxtrot he punched a tiny star in the corner of my card. He's added a different shape for every lesson since. I can read our whole summer against a window.

mbm-1803.clue: I tune the first string to the street outside.
mbm-1803.quote: The bread seller whistles the same three notes every morning. I answer on my cuatro from the front step. One day he finished the whole melody and forgot to sell me a loaf.

mbm-1804.clue: The bellows have one red pleat for luck.
mbm-1804.quote: My aunt patched my vallenato accordion with a square of her old red skirt. When I pull it wide for her favorite run, that flash goes all the way across the room.

mbm-1805.clue: We give the smallest hill the grandest name.
mbm-1805.quote: I took my nephew up the rise behind the car park. I planted a feather at the top, and he named it Eagle Peak. We ate our summit sandwiches six feet above the picnic table.

mbm-1806.clue: I'm the moon with a sunrise up my sleeve.
mbm-1806.quote: Our play needed daybreak, but the lamp was stuck on night. I opened my moon cape and showed the little yellow sun I'd sewn inside. At the next performance the little stars asked to see my sunrise again.

mbm-1807.clue: I'm saving the ball with the crescent bite.
mbm-1807.quote: My ball hit the metal moon above hole nine and came back with a crescent bite out of one side. I keep it in a dish by the door. If anyone asks, I got that one into orbit.

mbm-1808.clue: The spare guitar pick is a family portrait.
mbm-1808.quote: My dad cut me a pick from an expired photo badge. If I turn it over between songs I can see his very serious mustache. It got me through a very nervous first gig.

mbm-1809.clue: I practice with the lid open.
mbm-1809.quote: Our kitchen pot rings at almost exactly the first note of my part. I tap the rim with a spoon before choir. The neighbors must think we eat soup at very odd hours.

mbm-1810.clue: The room went very quiet when I picked up the pear.
mbm-1810.quote: I modeled in a green dress for the drawing group, holding a pear on my open palm. At the first break everyone showed me their sketches. Twenty versions of the pear, and one very patient wrist.

mbm-1811.clue: I quilted the long way round the needle.
mbm-1811.quote: I promised my left-handed cousin we'd make a quilt together. We sat at opposite ends of the long kitchen bench and stitched toward the middle. The crooked star is where our elbows finally met.

mbm-1812.clue: We stop the set when the pencil rolls.
mbm-1812.quote: My brother and I take our lifting rest on an old sloping bench. He sets my pencil at the high end and lets it roll. I catch it before it falls and write down the last set.

mbm-1813.clue: I keep the chilly end of the map.
mbm-1813.quote: We split the trail map at the fold by accident. My sister carried the sunny half and I took the shady slopes. We clipped it together at the lodge and raced two mugs of cocoa down the creases.

mbm-1814.clue: We brought a desk lamp to anime club.
mbm-1814.quote: I held it over our drawings of a city while my friends shaded the same giant robot. We moved the lamp one inch for every drawing. By tea time we'd made a whole sunset.

mbm-1815.quote: The top of a broken chess queen got too hot in the afternoon sun. My little sister folded a paper hat for it. Now our queen goes to the park dressed better than I do.

mbm-1816.clue: I always draw the thing next to the famous thing.
mbm-1816.quote: Beside the museum's big bronze horse was a plain wooden stool the sculptor had stood on. I sketched its paint-splashed legs. You could see exactly how high she'd had to reach.

mbm-1817.clue: My cousin keeps the long note for me.
mbm-1817.quote: When I change strings on my cuatro, she hums the last note I played so we can find our way back. Sometimes the whole porch joins in and I take a little longer tying the knot.

mbm-1818.clue: I lost mini golf to the ticket seller.
mbm-1818.quote: The woman who sells our tickets can see the whole course from her booth. She called a bank shot through her little window. I tried it, sank it, and slid the pencil over so she could take the credit.

mbm-1819.clue: I think the projectionist knew my grandfather.
mbm-1819.quote: We watched the last matinee of the week from Grandpa's favorite row. When the lights came up, a square of white light lingered on his old seat. I left my ticket there.

mbm-1820.quote: A radio operator called during a downpour and I could hear each drop hit his tin awning. I answered from my dry little room and tapped a pencil on the sill. We had ourselves a weather duet.

mbm-1821.clue: There's half a feather in my sketchbook.
mbm-1821.quote: The nuthatch I was drawing went behind a branch, and I left the blank part for next time. On the next page my daughter drew what she imagined was hidden. Her bird has striped trousers.

mbm-1822.clue: I keep the wrong side pretty, too.
mbm-1822.quote: I quilted a blue train for my brother. He turned it over and loved the crisscrossing threads on the back because they looked like a railway yard. We shipped it with two fronts.

mbm-1823.clue: I borrow a small patch of shade for my radio.
mbm-1823.quote: I like the warm stones at the edge of the beach. My straw hat spends the afternoon on the radio so the dial stays cool. By the evening the brim smells like the sea.

mbm-1824.clue: I buy the postcard after I draw the place.
mbm-1824.quote: In a hill town I sketched a crooked stair with nine flowerpots. The shopkeeper's postcard showed the same stair years ago with one pot. He pointed out which one had started the family.

mbm-1825.clue: I bring two discs for the long grass.
mbm-1825.quote: We sent a blue disc into a meadow and threw a yellow one to mark the spot. When we went to retrieve them a butterfly was sitting exactly where the colors overlapped.
